verdict_text: NO. The script sets `DROP = {2, 6, 10, 15}`, so it deletes block 15 and keeps block 14, violating Required result clause 1 ("Remove every tensor of blocks 2, 6, 10, 14"). Consequently the renumbering is also wrong: old block 14 is mapped to new index 11, whereas clause 2 requires old 15 → 11 (and old 14 to be removed), so the output's last block holds the wrong weights and grading against the reference will fail on bit-exact values. The built-in assertions do not catch this, since they only verify that the surviving indices form `range(12)` and that the tensor count is 184, both of which hold for the wrong drop set; in particular the specified check "no tensor of blocks 12, 13, 14, 15 remains" is only satisfied incidentally by renumbering, not by dropping the correct blocks.
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm). verdict none = no answer, excluded from rates.
